source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.229
purpose: Boundaries any downstream record must keep so that no result is widened beyond the author's stated setting. Every item is anchored to line numbers; none is a correctness judgement.
reference_convention: The anchor_labels fields hold either the author's stable \label value (e.g. thm_isometry) or, when the environment has no \label, the result key used in out/STRUCTURE_INDEX.json (prefixed r_, e.g. r_conj_ke). Printed numbers are never used: the effect of the \Subsection macro on the subsection counter was not verified by rendering.

necessary_conditions.statement: π:X→D* is a proper holomorphic submersion with projective fibers carrying a relatively ample line bundle L, and (X,L) admits an analytic model: a normal complex analytic space X̄, flat and proper over D̄, with X≅π^{-1}(D̄*) and an ample L̄ restricting to L.
necessary_conditions.why_needed: Logarithmic growth is defined by extending psh to a model, and the base-side pluripotential theory needs the disc compactification. Nothing covers a base of dimension >1 or a non-normal model.

necessary_conditions.statement: L and every L_i used in a pairing or an energy is relatively ample, not merely relatively nef or big.
necessary_conditions.why_needed: The Deligne pairing, the rooftop/Perron envelopes and the Bergman-kernel approximation all use relative ampleness; relative nefness appears only in the definition of non-Archimedean model metrics (def_defpsh).

necessary_conditions.statement: A reference boundary datum φ_∂, the restriction to π^{-1}(S^1) of a smooth psh metric on L, is fixed once and for all; E^1(L) is defined with this datum and ̂E^1(L) inherits it.
necessary_conditions.why_needed: The author states that this is what turns the Lelong-number construction into a genuine metric rather than a pseudometric; without it an additive boundary-supremum error appears (see the remark after lem_unifcontrol, line 738).

necessary_conditions.statement: Members of PSH(L) do not restrict to −∞ on a given fiber.
necessary_conditions.why_needed: Fiberwise finite energy and the fiberwise distance are undefined on an identically −∞ fiber.

necessary_conditions.statement: ̂E^1(L) consists of those E^1(L) metrics that are relatively maximal in the Sadullaev sense on every π^{-1}(U) with U relatively compact in D*.
necessary_conditions.why_needed: The metrization and the rooftop subharmonicity argument hold only on this locus. On all of E^1(L) the author constructs only a pseudodistance (prop_envelope and its corollary) and notes that the envelope does not a priori extend (the remark at line 854).

necessary_conditions.statement: Logarithmic growth means: there exists a model to which φ extends as a psh metric; equivalently, for every model and smooth reference metric, ρ^*φ≤φ^ref+O(log|z|).
necessary_conditions.why_needed: Without it neither the Lelong-number distance nor the (·)^NA map is defined. The author notes that maximality plus finite energy alone no longer gives logarithmic growth in this relative setting (exa_reldim, line 629).

necessary_conditions.statement: K=C((t)) with the t-adic valuation, R=C[[t]]; divisorial points come from irreducible components of central fibers of models, with normalization ord_E(·)/a_i for X̄_0=Σa_iE_i.
necessary_conditions.why_needed: Both the valuation and the normalizing multiplicity a_i enter the Lelong-number formula and the non-Archimedean energies; the results are stated for this field only.

necessary_conditions.statement: Non-Archimedean finite energy E^1(L_K^an) is finiteness of the non-Archimedean Monge–Ampère energy, extended by decreasing limits of continuous psh metrics; d_1^NA uses the non-Archimedean rooftop envelope.
necessary_conditions.why_needed: The isometry statement compares d_1^NA with ̂d_1 on this class only.

quantifiers_and_regularity.statement: Several statements are first proved for continuous metrics and then extended 'as usual from regularization' (for instance the pairing identity inside thm_isometry, line 1200); the interpolation step is not written out.
quantifiers_and_regularity.handling: Keep the author's quantifier over general metrics, but mark the regularization passage as author-omitted, not as an explicit derivation.

quantifiers_and_regularity.statement: Uniqueness in thm_uniquenesstropmaxdisc is uniqueness within ̂E^1(L) with fixed φ_∂ and prescribed non-Archimedean limit. Uniqueness in thm_existencemaximal is for continuous psh metrics with prescribed boundary values on π^{-1}(∂Ω).
quantifiers_and_regularity.handling: Never state uniqueness without the class and the boundary prescription.

quantifiers_and_regularity.statement: thm_existencemaximal point (1) is conditional on the existence of a continuous psh extension; existence is supplied only in point (2) under hyperconvexity of Ω.
quantifiers_and_regularity.handling: The two points must not be merged into an unconditional existence statement.

quantifiers_and_regularity.statement: Decreasing approximating families are nets in the general model discussion (lines 1133, 1152) and sequences where Demailly regularization is used (lines 306, 442, 599).
quantifiers_and_regularity.handling: Preserve net/sequence as written; convergence arguments cite continuity along decreasing limits accordingly.

quantifiers_and_regularity.statement: Completeness is for the base-locally uniform fiberwise d_1 topology on π^{-1}(U), U relatively compact in D*, which is shown equivalent to the ̂d_1 topology; a finer C^0_{X,loc}-d_1 topology is also introduced but not used for completeness.
quantifiers_and_regularity.handling: Do not upgrade completeness to the finer topology.

quantifiers_and_regularity.statement: ν_0 is a signed generalized Lelong number of a subharmonic function of at most logarithmic growth, normalized with an auxiliary a and independent of the admissible a.
quantifiers_and_regularity.handling: Keep the sign and the growth hypothesis; a bare 'Lelong number' is a different object.

object_boundaries.statement: ̂E^1(L) lives over D* and the metric is a Lelong number at 0; the central fiber X̄_0 enters only through models, vertical divisors and their valuations. No property of the general fiber is transferred to X̄_0, and no metric space structure on the central fiber is constructed.
object_boundaries.handling: A record must not describe the results as metrics on the central fiber or as a degeneration of metric spaces.

object_boundaries.statement: E^1(L) is the relative class E^1_{X/D*}(L) restricted to logarithmic growth with fixed boundary data; the fiberwise condition alone in r_def_relef is not membership in E^1(L).
object_boundaries.handling: Keep the two classes distinct when citing the Deligne-pairing extension (relative class) versus the metrization (with growth and boundary data).

object_boundaries.statement: The isometry identifies E^1(L_K^an) with ̂E^1_hyb(L), which is in general a proper locus of ̂E^1(L), characterized by equality in the energy–Lelong inequality.
object_boundaries.handling: Do not present ̂E^1_hyb(L) as all of ̂E^1(L).

object_boundaries.statement: The Lelong number of E(φ) depends on the chosen trivialization τ of ⟨L̄^{d+1}⟩; the author packages all such numbers as a non-Archimedean metric (rem_namap) rather than as a single number.
object_boundaries.handling: A record must not quote 'the' slope as an invariant without the trivialization or the non-Archimedean metric.

limit_and_normalization_points.statement: For S^1-invariant data identified with a convex function g̃ of t=log r, the slope at infinity equals MINUS ν_0(g); this explains the minus sign in the ̂d_1 definition.
limit_and_normalization_points.handling: Sign conventions must travel with any quoted distance formula.

limit_and_normalization_points.statement: Line 670 defines ̂d_1 := −ν_0(d_1(·,·)) while the theorem statement at line 674 and the abstract use ν_0 without the minus sign; line 119 in the introduction also arranges the signs of d_{1,z} differently from line 255.
limit_and_normalization_points.handling: Recorded as a literal source phenomenon for Codex; no correction, no independent resolution, and no conclusion about which sign the author intends.

limit_and_normalization_points.statement: E(φ_0,φ_1) is normalized by 1/((c_1(L)^d)(d+1)) and the pairing identity is (d+1)E(φ_0,φ_1)=⟨φ_0^{d+1}⟩−⟨φ_1^{d+1}⟩.
limit_and_normalization_points.handling: Any comparison with other normalizations of the Monge–Ampère energy must account for this factor.

limit_and_normalization_points.statement: ord_E(φ)=−sup{c≥0 : φ+a log|z| ≤ c φ_E + O(1) near E}+a, with φ_E locally log|f_E|+O(1) for a local equation f_E of E.
limit_and_normalization_points.handling: Keep the +a shift and the O(1); dropping them changes the metric.

limit_and_normalization_points.statement: The rooftop identity passes through lim_{r→0} of averages over rS^1 divided by log r, i.e. a slope in log r rather than a pointwise limit of functions.
limit_and_normalization_points.handling: A record must not replace the slope by a limit of the functions themselves.

boundaries_summary: Every candidate is confined to a proper holomorphic submersion over D* with relatively ample L admitting a normal analytic model, with logarithmic growth, fixed smooth psh boundary data on π^{-1}(S^1), fiberwise finite energy, and (for the metric structure) relative maximality. The non-Archimedean side is confined to K=C((t)) and to divisorial valuations from central fibers of models. Nothing extends to the central fiber as a metric object, nothing extends to non-maximal metrics beyond the explicit pseudodistance, and the energy identity is only an inequality outside the hybrid maximal locus. The open conjecture, the author-omitted steps and the literal notational anomalies are listed separately and must not be converted into results.

producer_recomputation_boundaries.statement: The new core of the complex side is the subharmonicity-with-log-growth of the rooftop pairing distance plus the uniform bound and the closedness of ̂E^1(L). Fiberwise Darvas completeness and fiberwise d_1 geometry are imported from [darbook] and are NOT new.
producer_recomputation_boundaries.handling: Do not count fiberwise Darvas theory, the definition of d_1, or the rooftop envelope as contributions of this work.

producer_recomputation_boundaries.statement: The new core of the non-Archimedean side is the construction of (·)^NA from multiplier ideals with a uniform generation shift, the decreasing subsequence via subadditivity, the two-boundary envelope with the energy–Lelong inequality, and the rooftop Lelong-number identity. The comparison ν_E(J(mφ))≤ν_E(φ)≤ν_E(J(mφ))+A_X(ν_E) is imported from [bbj].
producer_recomputation_boundaries.handling: Attribute the log-discrepancy comparison and the test-configuration dictionary to the cited sources, not to this paper.

producer_recomputation_boundaries.statement: prop_functionals (plurifunctional extension) is proved only in sketch form, with the quantitative estimate I_i≤C d_1^{2^{-n}}D(z) taken from [bbj, Lem. A.2] and the I-term bounds from [liytd, S4]; prop_testconf leaves distance preservation to the reader and cites [bbj, Th. 6.6].
producer_recomputation_boundaries.handling: These are cited-input results, neither candidates nor author-complete proofs.

producer_recomputation_boundaries.statement: The relative-dimension-zero examples (exa_reldim, exa_reldim2) and the S^1-invariant/test-configuration examples are illustrations and reductions, not new theorems.
producer_recomputation_boundaries.handling: Do not split them into candidates; they explain why the relative setting differs from the ray setting.

producer_recomputation_boundaries.statement: Remarks restating the dictionary (relative maximality = geodesic for S^1-invariant metrics; hybrid maximal = maximal geodesic ray) are terminology bridges to [bbj] and [darlurays], not results.
producer_recomputation_boundaries.handling: Do not count them as independent statements; Xia's alternative distance and the generalisation of her envelope are explicitly outside the article's scope (line 1271).

producer_author_unexpanded_or_open.statement: The concluding conjecture: for a degeneration of Calabi–Yau manifolds, ψ^NA=P(φ)^NA=Φ^NA, where ψ^NA is the non-Archimedean metric obtained by Boucksom–Jonsson from limits of the measures MA(φ_z).
producer_author_unexpanded_or_open.handling: Open; must never be indexed as a proved conclusion.

producer_author_unexpanded_or_open.statement: The author says it is likely that Xia's envelope construction generalises to metrics in ̂E^1(L) in this setting, 'although this is outside the scope of the present article'.

The maximal-envelope construction (prop_envelope) does not a priori extend to all of E^1(L) because of convergence problems for Lelong numbers under decreasing limits; a slightly larger class is described informally.
producer_author_unexpanded_or_open.handling: The pseudodistance is asserted only on C^0∩E^1(L); do not extend it.

producer_author_unexpanded_or_open.statement: The 'hybrid almost Kähler–Einstein' problem and the Calabi–Yau discussion at the end are posed as directions, together with a question about detecting families of KE metrics via non-Archimedean tools.

Three passages are explicitly incomplete by the author's own words: the plurifunctional extension 'we sketch now' (1284), the test-configuration distance preservation 'we leave to the interested reader' (1342), and the convex-to-subharmonic adaptation in the envelope proof (828).
producer_author_unexpanded_or_open.handling: Record as author-omitted; these must not be filled in or presented as complete author proofs.
